holidays.name: Popeye Day
holidays.description: Pull on your sailor cap and flex your forearms. This day honors the spinach-loving sailor man with the anchor tattoos and the squinty grin. Celebrate with a can of spinach, a cartoon marathon, or your best Popeye voice.
holidays.origin: Popeye first appeared in Elzie Segar's comic strip Thimble Theatre on January 17, 1929. He began as a minor character and became so popular that he took over the strip.
holidays.funFact: Popeye became so popular that spinach sales reportedly jumped in the United States, and a Texas town famous for growing spinach put up a statue of him.

holidays.name: National Hot Buttered Rum Day
holidays.description: This is a cozy day for sipping a warm mug of rum, butter, brown sugar, and spices. It's the drink to have when winter is at its coldest and you want to stay by the fire.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits the middle of January, when warm drinks are most welcome.
holidays.funFact: Hot buttered rum goes back to colonial America, when rum was a popular spirit and warm mixed drinks were a common way to fight the winter chill.

holidays.name: Kid Inventors' Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates young people who come up with creative ideas. It encourages kids to tinker, doodle and invent, and to build the gadgets in their heads.
holidays.origin: The day was created to mark the birthday of Benjamin Franklin, born January 17, 1706. Franklin was an inventor himself, and he is also linked to a famous invention made by a young person: the earmuffs created by 15-year-old Chester Greenwood.
holidays.funFact: Chester Greenwood patented his earmuffs at 19 after he invented them at 15 to keep his ears warm while ice skating.
